listenings.text: You asked how we got here, so let me give you the short version. When I joined, we used to do everything on paper. Filing cabinets, physical delivery, the lot. We used to work only with Brazilian companies, and honestly we did not use to think about anything else. Then in 2015 we took on our first foreign client, almost by accident, and they needed every report in English, every month. That one client changed the direction of the firm. It took us about three years to rebuild the processes around it. I tell you this because you are about to hand us something important, and I think you want to know that we have changed before and survived it.

Before I ask you anything, let me tell you how it worked here. One person used to run our entire payroll. She had been with us for nineteen years and she knew everything, which was wonderful until it was not. Every December she used to work both weekends, and nobody ever questioned it, because it always came out right. She retired in March. We did not replace her, partly because we could not find anyone, and partly because we realised we should not be in that position in the first place. So that is where we are. I am not really shopping for a price.

paras: The firm opened in 1992 with three people and a filing cabinet. It used to do bookkeeping for shops and small clinics in the same neighbourhood, and it did not use to take clients from outside the city.

In 2008 the founder's daughter joined and pushed for a computer system. The transition took four years and nearly split the partnership. Two of the older partners left. The ones who stayed later said it was the decision that saved the firm.

The real shift came in 2015, with a foreign client nobody had gone looking for. They needed reports in English, on a fixed calendar, with an audit trail. The firm had outgrown its legacy system without noticing, and rebuilding it took another three years.

Today the firm employs eighty people and serves a hundred and forty companies. What the partners tell prospects is not that they are big. It is that they have changed once already, on purpose, and know exactly what it costs.
